name: AiSOC v20 AI Security Operations Center
description: Ingest security alerts, correlate threats and triage them with AI agents.

PORT.description: Port the Next.js console listens on (the image starts it with -p 3000); Railway routes the public domain and its healthcheck here.

AISOC_DEMO_MODE.description: Demo mode off: the console never shows seeded demo data or the demo banner. Keep false.

API_URL.description: Core API on the private network. The console proxies /api/v1/* and /auth/* here server-side, so the API needs no public domain.

AGENTS_URL.description: Agents service on the private network (copilot, hunts, playbooks routes).

REALTIME_URL.description: Realtime gateway on the private network (WebSocket /ws and SSE /sse are proxied here).

ENRICHMENT_URL.description: Deliberately unreachable. The console has no caller of /api/v1/enrichment/*, and that rewrite would otherwise expose the unauthenticated enrichment service through the public console.

api.preDeployCommand: /bin/bash -c 'n=0; until python -m app.scripts.run_migrations; do n=$((n+1)); if [ "$n" -ge 5 ]; then echo "[railway] database migrations failed 5 times, giving up" >&2; exit 1; fi; echo "[railway] migrations failed (Postgres may still be starting), retry $n/5 in 15s" >&2; sleep 15; done; python -m app.scripts.bootstrap_admin || exit 1; end=$((SECONDS+300)); for hp in ${AISOC_RAILWAY_WAIT_FOR:-}; do until (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/${hp%:*}/${hp##*:}") 2>/dev/null; do if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$end" ]; then echo "[railway] $hp not reachable yet, continuing" >&2; break; fi; sleep 5; done; done; exit 0'

PORT.description: Port the API listens on (dual-stack); Railway's healthcheck probes it.

ENVIRONMENT.description: Production posture: the development auth bypass is unreachable and insecure defaults refuse to boot. Do not change.

AISOC_DEV_MODE.description: Development mode off: routes never fall back to an anonymous or demo principal. Do not change.

AISOC_PUBLISHED_BIND_ADDRS.description: Tells the service it is reachable from other hosts, so the developer auth shim stays refused even if dev mode were switched on.

AISOC_ALLOW_CLEARTEXT_KAFKA.description: Allow PLAINTEXT Kafka in production: the broker is reachable only over Railway's private network, which Railway encrypts. Set KAFKA_SECURITY_PROTOCOL instead if you bring a TLS broker.

AISOC_ADMIN_EMAIL.description: Sign-in e-mail of the first administrator, created by the pre-deploy step on the first deploy. Change it before deploying if you like (must be a syntactically valid address; .local/.test are rejected).

AISOC_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: Password of the first administrator (generated, 24 characters). Copy it from here to sign in; changing this variable later does not change an existing account (reset with `python -m app.scripts.bootstrap_admin --reset-password` in the api service shell).

SECRET_KEY.description: HS256 key for console sessions, shared by every service that verifies a console token (generated).

JWT_SECRET.description: HS256 key for SAML/OIDC session tokens, shared with ingest (generated; required in production).

AISOC_CREDENTIAL_KEY.description: Fernet key (32 bytes, url-safe base64) that encrypts connector credentials at rest; shared with connectors and actions (generated). Never change it after connectors are saved; rotate with AISOC_CREDENTIAL_KEY_ROTATION_FROM.

AISOC_SERVICE_TOKEN.description: Shared bearer for service-to-service calls and connector pushes to ingest (generated).

AISOC_API_SERVICE_TOKEN.description: Bearer a peer service presents to the API (agent customer tools, lake pivots, hunts) (generated).

AISOC_AGENTS_SERVICE_TOKEN.description: Bearer between the API and the agents service (triage context, MCP tools, SIEM writeback) (generated).

AISOC_ACTIONS_SERVICE_TOKEN.description: Bearer that gates every response action on the actions service (generated). Kept separate from the shared token on purpose.

AISOC_REALTIME_JWT_SECRET.description: HS256 key for realtime WebSocket/SSE tickets; the API mints, realtime verifies (generated).

AISOC_APP_DB_PASSWORD.description: Password of the aisoc_app runtime database role (DML only, row-level security applies). The pre-deploy migration step creates the role and sets this password (generated).

DATABASE_URL.description: Runtime connection as aisoc_app, TLS required (Railway Postgres serves TLS).

DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL.description: Owner connection used only by the pre-deploy migration runner for DDL, TLS required.

AISOC_MIGRATIONS_STRICT.description: Fail the deploy if any SQL migration fails, instead of booting on a partial schema.

KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS.description: Kafka-API broker (Redpanda) on the private network.

CONNECTORS_SERVICE_URL.description: Connectors service (catalog, test connection, federated search).

FUSION_SERVICE_URL.description: Fusion service behind the API's authenticated fusion gateway (entity risk, ML status).

AISOC_ACTIONS_BASE_URL.description: Actions service, where an approved response action is executed.

INGEST_SERVICE_URL.description: Ingest service on the private network.

INGEST_PUBLIC_URL.description: Public ingest URL shown in the setup wizard's push-URL examples. The sample-data button also posts here. Update after adding a custom domain to ingest.

LLM_GATEWAY_URL.description: LiteLLM gateway that resolves every aisoc-* model alias.

LITELLM_MASTER_KEY.description: Bearer the API presents to the LiteLLM gateway.

OPENAI_API_KEY.description: Optional hosted-provider key (empty = local model only). Set it on the litellm service; this references it.

AISOC_OLLAMA_URL.description: Local Ollama server, probed by the console's 'Deployment & AI' page.

AISOC_CONSOLE_URL.description: Console origin printed by the admin bootstrap and used in links.

CONSOLE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL.description: Console origin for share/invite links and OAuth return URLs. Update after adding a custom domain to web.

OAUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL.description: Base URL advertised as the OAuth redirect for connector sign-in (the console proxies /api/v1/oauth/callback to the API).

PASSKEY_RP_ID.description: WebAuthn relying-party id: the console host name. Update after adding a custom domain.

PASSKEY_RP_ORIGINS.description: WebAuthn origins as a JSON list (the console origin).

RETRO_HUNT_ENABLED.description: Retro-hunt sweeps over stored history (cost and privacy decision; off as upstream).

OTEL_EXPORTER.description: Tracing exporter off (no OpenTelemetry collector in this template).

AISOC_RAILWAY_WAIT_FOR.description: Template helper: the pre-deploy step waits (up to 5 minutes in total, non-fatal) until these host:port pairs accept connections, so the API starts with its graph and lake connections available on a first deploy.

ingest.startCommand: /bin/sh -c 'i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 36 ]; do wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null "$AISOC_RAILWAY_WAIT_URL" && break; i=$((i+1)); sleep 5; done; exec ./ingest-service'

PORT.description: Port Railway routes the public domain and healthcheck to (same as HTTP_PORT).

ENV.description: Read before ENVIRONMENT by ingest's mode check. Production requires JWT_SECRET and disables development shortcuts. Do not change.

AISOC_ALLOW_CLEARTEXT_KAFKA.description: Allow PLAINTEXT Kafka on Railway's encrypted private network.

DATABASE_DSN.description: Postgres (pgx DSN, TLS required) used to resolve minted push tokens and mount the /v1/inbox/* webhook routes.

JWT_SECRET.description: Same JWT secret as the API (ingest refuses to start without one in production).

AISOC_SERVICE_TOKEN.description: Shared service token; accepted on /v1/ingest only together with an X-Tenant-ID header naming an active tenant.

ATTCK_DATA_PATH.description: Upstream's path for the ATT&CK bundle. The published image does not contain it, so technique enrichment at ingest is off (upstream behaviour, logged as a warning); detections and the agents still map techniques.

AISOC_GRAPH_ENABLED.description: Write entities to the Neo4j graph at ingest (upstream 'full' profile).

AISOC_CORS_ORIGINS.description: Allowed browser origin (the console). Telemetry senders are not browsers and are unaffected.

AISOC_RAILWAY_WAIT_URL.description: Template helper: ingest waits up to 3 minutes for Neo4j at start, because its graph writer disables itself for the life of the process if Neo4j is not reachable within 60 s.

AISOC_LLM_MODEL_FAST.description: Model behind the high-volume aliases (triage, summary, copilot, NL, hunt, detection). Any LiteLLM model string, e.g. openai/<model> with OPENAI_API_KEY set and AISOC_LLM_API_BASE emptied.

AISOC_LLM_MODEL_DEEP.description: Model behind the investigation and report aliases.

AISOC_LITELLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds the gateway waits for one generation. 300 suits CPU-only inference (upstream default 60, raised per upstream issue #1241 guidance).

PORT.description: Port Ollama listens on; Railway's healthcheck probes it.

OLLAMA_PULL_MODELS.description: Models pulled on first boot (comma-separated). Upstream's pinned CPU model, about 2 GB.

OLLAMA_BASE_MODEL.description: Model the CPU-tuned copy is created from.

OLLAMA_DEFAULT_MODEL.description: CPU-tuned copy (explicit thread count and context) that the LiteLLM aliases use. Recreated on every start.

OLLAMA_NUM_THREAD.description: Optional override for the inference thread count. Empty = the service's CPU quota, capped at 8.

OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH.description: Context window of the tuned model (tokens).

OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE.description: 8-bit KV cache (about half the memory of f16).

OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL.description: One generation at a time (CPU); other requests queue.

OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS.description: Keep at most one model in memory.

OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE.description: Unload the model after 30 idle minutes (frees about 2.5 GB).

kafka.startCommand: /bin/sh -c "rm -rf /var/lib/redpanda/data/lost+found && exec rpk redpanda start --kafka-addr internal://[::]:9092 --advertise-kafka-addr internal://$RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN:9092 --pandaproxy-addr internal://[::]:8082 --advertise-pandaproxy-addr internal://$RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN:8082 --schema-registry-addr internal://[::]:8081 --rpc-addr 0.0.0.0:33145 --advertise-rpc-addr $RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN:33145 --mode dev-container --smp 1 --memory $REDPANDA_MEMORY --reserve-memory 0M --default-log-level=info"

PORT.description: Redpanda admin API port; Railway's healthcheck probes /v1/status/ready here.

REDPANDA_MEMORY.description: Memory Redpanda may use (Seastar would otherwise size itself to the host). Raise with the service's RAM.

RAILWAY_RUN_UID.description: Run as root so Redpanda can write the root-owned Railway volume.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Allow a clean shutdown on redeploy.
